newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bill rates end sharply lower as TWI hits highs.
newsitem.headline: NZ bill rates end sharply lower as TWI hits highs.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.75 PCT (PREV 7.85) US 5-YR 6.27 (PREV 6.33)
* NZ bank bills rally strongly as TWI posts fresh 9-yr highs
* Money market looking for positive CPI number next week
* Flows light in long end as investors await U.S. data
Short term wholesale interest rates fell sharply in New Zealand on Friday as the Kiwi dollar continued to strengthen, its Trade-Weighted Index shooting to fresh nine-year highs.
"At the moment it's apparently a one-way bet to any foreign investor wanting to chuck money into New Zealand," said a money market trader.
"They throw money into a very strong currency that's still earning a healthy seven percent-plus rate right out across the curve."
As the TWI rose above 68.30, posting its highest levels since late 1987, the 90-day bank bill rate fell 17 basis points to 7.50 percent.

Dealers said the money market was also looking for a positive inflation number from next Friday's Consumer Price Index and the 90-day bills could continue to rally, although some profit-taking was on the cards.
"There'll probably be some profit-taking at these levels -- 7.5 percent is quite a psychological barrier," the trader said.
Bond dealers said the short-dated bonds had benefited from the strength in the bills, with a good bid tone in the 97s, 98s and 2000s.
"I wouldn't be surprised if there was some sort of dual currency or samurai-type issuance as well," a dealer said.
The long end of the curve struggled over the course of the day, although volumes were minimal as investors waited for U.S. nonfarms payrolls data due tonight.

"If you get a strong number over there, the interest rate market is going to get a real pounding, so I don't think anyone's really prepared to commit themselves until after they've seen that," the dealer said.
